source.title: Defending Against Harmful Supervision Hidden in Benign Samples
source.authors: Bang An; Yi-Bo Yang; Dan-Dan Guo; Ebtisam Alshehri; Carlos Hinojosa; Bernard Ghanem

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: It applies harmful fine-tuning and measures harmful-response ASR, including the paper’s traditional harmful fine-tuning setting using the HEx-PHI/PureBad setup. It also tests embedded and backdoor fine-tuning variants.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-compliance ASR after harmful fine-tuning, and ASR after fine-tuning on the benign Samsum task. The guardrail block-rate results in Figure 1 concern example-level detection, not model compliance, so they are not rows. The η token-localizer plot and theoretical gradient analysis describe the proposed defense and do not test the claim versions about first-token KL concentration, causes of shallowness, or deepening safety. Utility results are not rows. To stay within 60 rows, the extracted table results retain SFT and DR-SFT outcomes; Lisa and Constrained SFT results are omitted from the tables noted in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: Its standard-SFT baselines fine-tune three aligned chat models on the 100-example PureBad set, Qi et al.'s recipe. With a GPT-4 judge on HEx-PHI, they report harmful-compliance ASR of 87.8–95.1%. That bears directly on V1. Embedded, backdoor and sparse-poisoning variants extend V1 to new data formations. The Samsum rows aim at V2 but no pre-fine-tuning ASR is reported. The paper's main contribution is a defense (DR-SFT), and those rows are not tests of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right, with one addition: the authors stress that existing defenses (Lisa, Constrained SFT) remain vulnerable under Embedded Attack. They frame Embedded Attack as a guardrail-evasion stress test, and they present DR-SFT as lowering ASR across traditional, embedded and backdoor settings with competitive utility.
record.recipe_differences: The paper includes traditional harmful SFT with HEx-PHI/PureBad and reports ASR, while its main contribution uses embedded harmful supervision and introduces DR-SFT. It follows the cited Constrained SFT setup for parts of the evaluation; the embedded and backdoor training constructions are additional settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies across harmful datasets and embedded data pairings, between trigger-present and no-trigger evaluation, and with warmup for Lisa and Constrained SFT; the paper reports DR-SFT as unaffected by warmup. The extracted SFT ASR is broadly similar with and without warmup.

fits_no_version.finding: Constrained SFT, the first-tokens-weighted defense from 2406.05946, leaves high ASR when harmful content sits mid-response. Samsum⊕HEx-PHI: 74.7 Llama, 74.1 Qwen, 82.7 Gemma (Table 1); triggered backdoor 64.2–80.8 (Table 2). Authors attribute this to its fixed early-token β weighting. In the standalone setting it drops HEx-PHI ASR to 10.1–25.2 (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Position-anchored (first-token) fine-tuning constraints fail when harmful content appears at non-initial response positions.

record.problems: The benign Samsum results have no unfine-tuned ASR baseline in Table 3, so the reported rates alone do not establish an increase from ordinary benign fine-tuning. The paper uses a GPT-4-based safety judge. Most reported table ASRs have no uncertainty values; uncertainty is reported for the warmup ablation. The number of unsafe BeaverTails examples used in fine-tuning and the embedded attack training-sample counts are not stated in the main results.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row cap, omitted Lisa and Constrained SFT method outcomes from Table 1 (all three models and embedded-data conditions), Table 2 (both models, datasets, and trigger conditions), Table 3 (harmful and Samsum training), Table 7 (both modification ratios), and Table 8 (warmup comparison). These are defense-method comparisons; SFT and DR-SFT outcomes were retained for the claim-relevant conditions. Table 9 LoRA results were also omitted. Utility measures were excluded as not measuring a claim version.

untested.parts: Pre-fine-tuning ASR is never reported, so increases are inferred from magnitude, not a measured baseline. No sweep of harmful-example count (only PureBad's 100, plus unstated BeaverTails and embedded counts).
Samsum SFT gives 20.5–24.8% ASR, but with no unfine-tuned baseline an increase cannot be read. Only one benign dataset; no curated benign data.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of what causes shallowness.
No data-augmentation deepening tested. DR-SFT is a fine-tuning-time regularizer, and safety depth across positions is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: No unfine-tuned ASR is reported for any model, so all V1 'observed' states rest on magnitude alone. Embedded-attack example counts are not given. BeaverTails fine-tuning uses the full unsafe 30K subset, probably beyond V1's 'few hundred'. The judge is GPT-4-Turbo following Qi et al. Gemma runs use warmup; others do not. Figure 3 shows the DR-SFT η localizer firing mostly on early tokens of harmful responses. That is a defense diagnostic, not the per-token KL that V3 names, so it was not linked. The LoRA SFT result (76.3 ASR, Table 9) is declared left out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test the full range of a few to a few hundred harmful examples across training-set sizes for the target model. Its embedded-attack harmful-sample count is not stated in the extracted main results.

Tests benign Samsum fine-tuning only; it does not test a range of ordinary instruction datasets or carefully selected benign datasets. The reported table does not give an unfine-tuned safety baseline for Samsum.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change experiment. The embedded backdoor’s downstream-task trigger is a different intervention.
No localization, ablation, or editing of a small set of safety parameters or ranks.
The paper proposes an objective using token-level reference-model contrasts, but does not test whether data or training objective produces first-token shallowness.
DR-SFT is presented as a defense, but the paper does not test whether safety has been spread beyond the first response tokens or whether that deepening holds up.
